name: What if my lot in Burbank has a slope or retaining wall issues?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a Burbank lot has slope, drainage, or retaining wall issues before new home construction starts?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a Burbank lot has slope, drainage, or retaining wall issues before new home construction starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a Burbank lot has slope, drainage, or retaining wall issues, the project usually needs more front-end planning before construction can begin. A geotechnical report, grading plan, and structural engineering often become essential, because the foundation and site drainage must match the soil and slope conditions. These issues can also trigger extra permit review and more inspections. The practical risk is budget creep: site work may cost far more than a homeowner expected, especially if access is tight or existing retaining walls must be repaired or replaced. Before you commit, ask for a site evaluation that includes excavation access, drainage path, soil conditions, and the likely need for retaining structures. A builder experienced with hillside or irregular lots can identify whether the home design should be adjusted early, which is far cheaper than redesigning after permit review or during excavation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Slope, drainage, and retaining wall problems can add engineering, geotechnical testing, and extra grading work before construction begins. These issues may change the foundation design, increase permit review time, and raise total project cost. On difficult lots, site prep can be one of the largest budget items.
